features.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
features.desc: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
body: While Garrett didn't record a sack Sunday, Donald got his first sack of the season — finishing with 1.5 to move ahead of Chandler Jones and Justin Houston for 31st.
Hunter missed his first game of the season, and the rest of the list failed to record a sack — with Mack and Campbell playing on "Monday Night Football."

In his first game since Week 1, Garrett made his presence felt. He had three sacks to move ahead of Dwight Freeney, Derrick Thomas and Rickey Jackson for 18th on the list. He was the only one of the active leaders to record a sack this week.
With two players on bye and Garrett out, only two of the five active players that played this week recorded sacks, but they were impactful.
Miller recorded his first sack as a Cowboy Sunday, moving him ahead of Terrell Suggs and into a tie with Jason Taylor for seventh.
Watt added two sacks of his own, moving him ahead of Simeon Rice and Clyde Simmons for 23rd. He now has 7.5 sacks on the season.
Hunter and Watt were the only ones to record sacks this week, with Hunter jumping back over Campbell in the rankings.
With Garrett still out, it was another quiet week on the sack front. Of the active leaders, it was the oldest that recorded the lone sack of the week in Campbell. He moved back in front of Hunter.
Hunter was the only player among the active leaders to record a sack this week, moving him ahead of Campbell to No. 26 all-time. Hunter now has three sacks through five games.

Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR.

features.headline: What's working — and not working — for LeBron James, Philadelphia 76ers
features.desc: We talked to several coaches, executives and scouts about the 11-3 Sixers in an attempt to get a consensus opinion on their start.
body: There are few people on the planet more qualified to speak about what it's like to be a part of a nascent LeBron James-led group with immediate super-team expectations than former NBA sharpshooter Mike Miller.

As a member of the Miami Heat for the first three years of the Heatles' run (2010-13) who again teamed up with James for the tumultuous first season of the superstar's second stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2014-15), Miller knows life in the LeBron pressure cooker.

"Everywhere he went, you would find out real quickly who's going to be able to step out there and who's not," said Miller, who now is an agent representing NBA players as the president of LIFT Sports Management. "It's different.
Every shot now, crowd-wise, everything becomes magnified. I've had some good success personally [before playing with James], but nothing on the level of where you really test yourself on that stage.
"That's the reason I chose Miami. I wanted to know if I was going to s—- myself, or perform?"
So far, for the most part, the Philadelphia 76ers have performed fantastically.

The Sixers won eight of their first nine games, including an opening-night victory at Madison Square Garden to spoil the New York Knicks' ring night. They came back from down 29 points to beat the Cavaliers.
And they went on the road to avenge a previous loss to the Detroit Pistons, last season's No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference.

But two blowout losses in their last five games in Cleveland — when James and Joel Embiid combined to shoot 3-for-21 and had eight turnovers — and at home against their longtime rivals in the Boston Celtics — which caused Jaylen Brown to admit afterward how frustrated he was by his showing — brought them back down to earth.

features.headline: Ranking men's college basketball All-American, player of the year candidates
features.desc: It's a wide-open race to crown the best players in the sport, led by Jeremy Fears Jr. Plus, under-the-radar names to know.
body: Two seasons ago, it didn't take long for the player of the year race to focus on Duke's Cooper Flagg and Auburn's Johni Broome. Last season was all about the freshmen, with Duke's Cameron Boozer and BYU's AJ Dybantsa sharing the spotlight before the season.

The 2026-27 race should be a bit more wide open. College basketball has a deeper talent pool than ever — mostly a byproduct of revenue sharing and higher salary caps that have led to potential first-round draft picks returning for another season.

European pros are also coming to the United States to play in college. And although the freshman class doesn't have the same star power as those of the past couple of seasons, there are several impactful first-year players.
So, we will lean into that depth of talent and track the potential All-Americans and player of the year candidates all season.

Not only will it include ranking the 10 best players in the country, but we'll also look at a handful of under-the-radar players who could break out and challenge for a spot on the first- or second-team All-America lists.
Here is where things stand after the first two weeks of the season.
Standout performance: 18 points, 7 rebounds, 11 assists vs. Duke (Champions Classic) on Nov. 10
It didn't take long for Fears to make his case as the best point guard — and player — in the country in the Spartans' 79-73 Champions Classic win against Duke in Chicago.

After the victory, coach Tom Izzo said he had challenged Fears during the week to live up to the preseason expectations, and Duke coach Jon Scheyer acknowledged that Fears "controlled the whole game." — Jeff Borzello

features.headline: Every MLB team's chance of signing Skubal — and their backup plans
features.desc: Dodger or Met blue? We break down all 30 clubs' chances of landing the offseason's biggest free agent — and who their Plan B should be.
body: Tarik Skubal is the golden ticket in the 2026-27 MLB free agent class. In what is viewed as a weak group of free agents, the two-time Cy Young Award winner is the clear difference-maker, a pitcher with a 2.42 ERA over the past three seasons.
The state of modern pitching is at an interesting inflection.

While starters are throwing harder than ever — with even more unhittable breaking balls and a wider variety of pitches — it is also arguably harder than ever to fill 162 starts in a season, let alone fill enough quality innings.
In 2026, 377 different pitchers started a game — an average of 12.6 per team — and Michael Wacha was the only pitcher to throw 200 innings.
Ten years ago, there were 310 different pitchers who started a game and 15 pitchers who reached 200 innings. Twenty years ago, those figures were 303 starters and 45 who reached 200 innings.
Forty years ago, it was 9.6 starters per team and 52 who pitched 200 innings — and a total of 82 who pitched 162 innings compared to just 46 in 2026.

You get the idea: An ace starter on Skubal's level is a special addition to any roster. Of course, with Skubal perhaps in line for a $300 million contract, not every team has the same odds of signing him — although, who knows, a new labor deal could drastically change how these deals unfold.

With that, let's introduce the Skubal Tiers — breaking all 30 teams into tiers on their likelihood of landing Skubal. And since every team needs pitching help of some sort, we'll include a reasonable backup pitching plan for each team.

features.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
features.desc: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
body: Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.
In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game.
Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.
On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks.
It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.
Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.
Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

features.headline: Who has scored the most goals in NHL history?
features.desc: Alex Ovechkin holds the record for the most individual career goals in NHL history. Which other players are at the top of the list?
body: At the time of his retirement in 1999, Wayne Gretzky owned or shared 61 NHL records, including the mark for the most career goals. "The Great One" finished his illustrious 20-year career with an NHL-record 894 goals in 1,487 games. It is a mark that stood until Alex Ovechkin broke it in April 2025.

With Gretzky in attendance, Ovechkin scored his 895th career goal in a 4-1 loss to the New York Islanders. Ovechkin's record-breaking goal came in the 1,487th game of his NHL career, the same as Gretzky's career total.
The 2026-27 NHL season marks the 22nd for Ovechkin, who looks to add to his career goals total and put even more separation between him and the rest of the field.
